properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 4 at 10:44AM EDT until September 4 at 11:45AM EDT by NWS Grand Rapids MI
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Nearshore and Open Waters from South Haven to Grand Haven MI...

At 1044 AM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 8 nm west of Grand Haven Light to 28 nm east of Wind
Pt., moving southeast at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Saugatuck Pier Heads, Port Sheldon Harbor, and Holland Light.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:22PM CDT until September 6 at 5:40AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Village Creek Near Kountze affecting Hardin County.

Pine Island Bayou Near Sour Lake affecting Jefferson and Hardin
Counties.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier affecting Jefferson,
Hardin, Jasper and Orange Counties.

For the Neches River...including Town Bluff, Evadale, Neches River
Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.
For the Village Creek...including Kountze...Moderate flooding is
forecast.
For the Pine Island Bayou...including Sour Lake...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Village Creek near Kountze.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Water covers entire floor of Farm to Market
Road 418. Water threatens homes near the creek in Kountze.
Significant flooding occurs in Village Creek State Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 22.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM CDT Thursday was 22.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 22.4 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
Saturday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 22.4
feet on 04/06/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 830 AM CDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 4:29PM CDT until September 4 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Hardin County in southeastern Texas...
Northwestern Jefferson County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 428 PM CDT, Gauge reports and emergency management are
reporting flooding continuing. Flooding is already occurring in
the warned area.
- Flood water are moving down Village Creek, Little Pine Island
Bayou and Pine Island Bayou.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Kountze, Sour Lake, Saratoga, Wildwood,
Thicket, Bevil Oaks, Honey Island, Village Mills, Batson and
Votaw.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Mississippi Sound; Chandeleur Sound; Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued September 4 at 8:38AM CDT until September 4 at 10:15AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Mississippi Sound...
Chandeleur Sound...
Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20
NM...

* Until 1015 AM CDT.

* At 838 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Long Beach, moving northwest at 5
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Ship Island, Mississippi Sound, Ocean Springs, Horn Island, Cat
Island, Biloxi, Pascagoula, Long Beach, Pass Christian, Bay St.
Louis and Waveland.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 3 at 11:26PM CDT until September 5 at 12:44PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Menard Creek near Rye affecting Liberty, Hardin and Polk Counties.

For the Menard Creek...including Rye...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Menard Creek near Rye.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding begins as
low-lying areas along the creek are inundated. At 28.0 feet, Major
lowland flooding begins with widespread inundation of the
floodplain in the vicinity of the gage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 27.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 17.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:15 PM CDT Thursday was 28.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Saturday morning and continue falling to 11.2 feet Tuesday
evening.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 04/21/1979.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued Friday evening at 1130 PM CDT.
